payload.meta_description: A printable honeymoon itinerary template and a two week sample plan, with the passport, visa, insurance and health checks Australians need before flying.
payload.excerpt: Plan the shape of your honeymoon before the places: a printable day-by-day honeymoon itinerary template, a two week sample built around rest days, two bases and one travel day, the work behind each transfer, and the official passport, visa, insurance and health checks for Australians, linked at the source.

payload.format_note: The template is a header block (four separate paragraphs) plus a native table block (8 columns, 14 day rows). Checklist lines are checklist or list blocks. Never paste the table as text or an image.
payload.categories_note: Travel Guides only. Set it as primary with 'Make primary'.
payload.author: [[NEEDS: named author]]
key_takeaways: Plan the shape of the honeymoon first (arrival and rest days, how many bases, which day you travel between them) and choose the places second.
Our two week sample uses two bases with a dedicated travel day between them, a gentle first two days and an open final morning before the flight home.
Check your passport validity and allow at least six weeks for a new one (see Documents below).
Choose travel insurance that covers every country on the trip, including stopovers and transit points, and check which activities the policy excludes.
Book the honeymoon in the name on the passport you will carry, and book a doctor's visit at least eight weeks before you fly.

faq.q: How many places should we visit on a two week honeymoon?
faq.a: Two bases is a comfortable rhythm for two weeks. Our sample uses two, with a dedicated transfer day whenever the base changes, so packing, checking out and travelling get a day of their own rather than crowding a holiday day.

faq.q: How many days should a honeymoon itinerary be?
faq.a: As a starting point, we suggest seven days with one base, rest first and a slow finish; ten days with two bases and one travel day; or three weeks, adding a third base only if each base gets four nights or more. Destination and season shape the rest.

faq.q: Should we plan every day of the honeymoon?
faq.a: Plan the shape, then leave space. We keep to one core experience a day, two at most, build in a rest day or half-day around the middle and leave the final morning open. Write every booking into the template so the unplanned hours can be exactly that.

faq.q: When should we start planning the honeymoon itinerary?
faq.a: Our package lead times put the ideal lead time for a honeymoon at six to nine months, to lock in the right suite category. Our seven-day trip planner suggests booking stays first, then flights and transfers, then private experiences and restaurants, and notes that these are indicative windows that vary by destination, season and experience.

faq.q: Can someone plan and book the whole itinerary for us?
faq.a: We plan the honeymoon as one connected trip: you share your travel window and the kind of trip you picture, choose from a tailored shortlist, and we coordinate transfers, dining, spa and private experiences so every reservation is in place when you arrive. Visa and entry rules stay yours to confirm with each embassy or consulate.
